item.title: Researchers Introduce CARing Framework to Improve LLM Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction
item.description:
Researchers Introduce CARing Framework to Improve LLM Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction

Researchers have developed CARing, a new framework designed to enhance next-visit diagnosis prediction in large language models (LLMs) by addressing multi-label coverage and tokenization challenges.

🔍 Overview

Large language models offer promising potential for next-visit diagnosis prediction due to their capacity to integrate and reason over longitudinal clinical evidence in natural language. However, conventional reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning typically rewards each trajectory based solely on the correctness of its final answer.

In next-visit diagnosis prediction, multiple diagnoses can be valid at the same time. Independently rewarding a single diagnosis per trajectory does not distinguish repeated hits from the coverage of different diagnoses, which can cause the model’s policy to concentrate on only a few correct diagnoses while leaving others uncovered. Furthermore, standard LLM tokenizers can split ICD codes into multiple generic tokens with limited clinical meaning, which requires multiple decoding steps to predict each diagnosis and hinders reasoning over large disease vocabularies.

🧩 How it works

To resolve these issues, the CARing framework introduces several technical approaches:

  • Compositional Semantic IDs (SIDs): Diagnoses are represented with compact SIDs, which encode ontology-enriched disease semantics through residual quantization.
  • Contextual Grounding: The resulting SID tokens are grounded in natural language and longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) contexts using multi-task alignment and reasoning-enriched training to unlock transferable LLM reasoning.
  • Coverage Reward and Supervision: Unordered multi-label prediction is improved through a coverage reward for reinforcement learning combined with multi-positive supervision.
  • Inference Flexibility: At inference time, the model supports both efficient direct constrained decoding and multi-chain reasoning with rank fusion.

⚙️ Key details

The CARing framework was evaluated on the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets, demonstrating the following performance results:

  • It exceeded all EHR-trained baselines in weighted F1.
  • It achieved the highest top-k recall at every reported cutoff.
  • In reasoning mode, it attained a Recall@30 (R@30) of 46.04% and 46.52%.

🚀 Availability

The codes and logs for the CARing framework are available online at the project’s repository URL.

#ClinicalAI #LLMs #Healthcare

Source: Coverage-Aware Reasoning with Medical Tokens for Diagnosis Prediction Source: Clinician use of language models diverges from how the models are evaluated

item.title: International Study Evaluates 11 AI Systems for Gum Disease Diagnosis
item.description:
International Study Evaluates 11 AI Systems for Gum Disease Diagnosis

On October 5, 2026, an international study led by Dr. Yaniv Mayer, senior physician and director of the residency program in the Department of Periodontics and Implants at Rambam and senior lecturer at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, Faculty of Medicine, was published in the Journal of Clinical Periodontology. The research examined, for the first time on a comparative basis, eleven leading artificial‑intelligence systems to see how they perform as auxiliary tools for diagnosing and treating gum disease.

🔍 Overview

  • The study compared 11 AI systems on their ability to diagnose gum diseases and recommend treatment.
  • It sought to determine which systems provide safer recommendations and which might endanger patients.
  • The work emphasizes that AI is becoming a working tool for professionals in fields such as medicine, where it can help achieve faster, more accurate, and more efficient diagnoses.

🦷 AI in Periodontics

  • Artificial intelligence is rapidly integrating into medical practice, including periodontics (gum health).
  • The study’s results highlight that expert oversight remains essential for safe patient care, even when AI tools are used.

📊 Study Details

  • Lead researcher: Dr. Yaniv Mayer (Senior physician, Department of Periodontics and Implants, Rambam; Senior lecturer, Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, Faculty of Medicine).
  • Publication: Journal of Clinical Periodontology.
  • Date: October 05, 2026.
  • Scope: Comparative evaluation of 11 leading AI systems for gum disease diagnosis and treatment recommendation.

💡 Why It Matters

  • The Technion has been Israel’s technological engine for more than 100 years, driving innovation, technology, and entrepreneurship.
  • By testing AI tools in dentistry, the study contributes to the broader effort of transforming ideas into impact across medicine and security.
  • Findings help clinicians understand the limits of AI, reinforcing the need for human expertise to ensure patient safety.

🚀 Looking Ahead

  • Continued collaboration between academic institutions (Technion, Rambam) and AI developers will shape how AI assists clinicians.
  • Ongoing research will be needed to refine AI recommendations and safeguard against potential risks.

Discover how AI performs in gum disease diagnosis and why expert oversight remains essential for safe patient care.

#AI #Periodontics #MedicalAI #Healthcare #Technion

Source: Can AI Safely Support Gum Disease Diagnosis?

item.title: Nolla Health launches AI‑driven acne prescription pilot in Utah
item.description:
Nolla Health launches AI‑driven acne prescription pilot in Utah

People in Utah can now use AI to get a prescription for acne treatment.

🔍 Overview

On Monday, healthcare startup Nolla Health announced that Utah residents can scan their faces with the company’s app. The AI system analyzes acne severity and autonomously writes a prescription, as reported by Bloomberg.

🧩 How it works

  • Users open the Nolla Health app and capture a facial scan.
  • The AI evaluates the scan for mild‑to‑moderate acne.
  • If the AI is confident, it selects one of eight skin‑treatment options and generates a prescription.
  • If the AI cannot “confidently select a treatment,” the user is directed to a physician.

⚙️ Key details

  • Physician oversight – The pilot starts with two physicians approving each AI‑generated prescription for the first 100 patients. Oversight relaxes after up to 500 prescriptions, then at least 10 % of prescriptions are reviewed each month plus any escalations or side‑effects.
  • First‑time prescriptions – Utah has allowed AI systems to renew certain medications earlier this year, but Nolla Health is the first in the country to issue initial prescriptions via AI.
  • Cost – The service is priced at $4.99 per month.
  • Eligibility – Available to Utah residents who are 18 years or older and have mild‑to‑moderate acne.
  • Treatment options – The AI can currently prescribe eight different skin treatments.
  • Purpose – The pilot is described as complementary to physicians, handling routine, low‑acuity cases so dermatologists can focus on complex, high‑risk patients.

🚀 Availability

The program launches as a pilot in Utah with gradual loosening of physician oversight as outlined above.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates a regulatory approval pathway for AI‑generated initial prescriptions.
  • Shows a model where AI handles routine dermatology cases, potentially reshaping dermatologist workload.
  • Provides a low‑cost, subscription‑based option for patients with mild acne.

#AI #Healthcare #Dermatology #Prescription #Utah

Source: This startup is issuing AI-generated acne prescriptions

item.title: Diagens Tech Unveils iMedImage Suite for Continuous Medical Imaging AI
item.description:
Diagens Tech Unveils iMedImage Suite for Continuous Medical Imaging AI

🔍 Overview

On Sept. 25, during the fifth Global Digital Trade Expo, Diagens Tech demonstrated how medical imaging data can drive AI‑enabled productivity. The company presented a four‑layer product suite that builds on its universal foundation model, iMedImage®, and showed more than 20 use cases across specialties such as obstetrics, cardiology, emergency care, and oncology.

🧩 Architecture

Layer Description
iMedImage® Large‑scale foundation model for medical imaging covering 43 organs/anatomical sites and 61 disease areas
iMedStudio™ Workspace for multimodal intelligent annotation, AI‑assisted image processing, expert review and quality control
iMedMaaS® Platform for training and deploying models for specific specialties
iMedLoop™ (includes DoctorBench®) Closed‑loop system linking data collaboration, evaluation, release and feedback

⚙️ How it works

  • Clinicians can participate in data annotation and correction through iMedStudio™, feeding professional expertise into ongoing model training.
  • iMedMaaS® trains specialty‑specific models on the foundation model’s knowledge.
  • iMedLoop™ continuously updates the production system, addressing the reality that clinical scenarios are neither standardized nor static.
  • AI AutoVision®, a karyotype‑assisted diagnostic software built on iMedImage®, has received Class III medical device registration from China’s NMPA.

📊 Key details

  • More than 3,000 professional annotators support the platform.
  • The underlying dataset contains 28.95 million medical imaging records.
  • The suite supports imaging modalities including CT, MRI, X‑ray, ultrasound, CTA and endoscopy.
  • Partnerships with 99 hospitals, including 65 Grade A tertiary hospitals.
  • Demonstrated >20 representative use cases spanning obstetrics & gynecology, growth & development, cardiovascular & cerebrovascular conditions, emergency & critical care, and oncology.

💡 Why it matters

Medical AI lacks a fixed set of standardized answers; clinicians may interpret the same scan differently, and new disease entities and diagnostic modalities constantly emerge. Diagens Tech’s closed‑loop workflow and customizable foundation model aim to keep AI tools up‑to‑date, allowing continuous, compliant model rebuilding as clinical knowledge evolves. This approach aligns with the view that future competition will focus on the ability to create tailored models efficiently and continuously.

#MedicalAI #FoundationModels #Healthcare #ImagingAI

Source: Hangzhou Diagens Biotechnology Silicon Valley “Godfather” Kevin Kelly: AI’s Core Asset Is the Ability to Keep Building New AI Systems

item.title: CliniCIRCA Framework for Temporal Reconstruction of Clinical Annals
item.description:
CliniCIRCA Framework for Temporal Reconstruction of Clinical Annals

Researchers have introduced CliniCIRCA, a multi-stage LLM framework designed for Calendar-anchored, Imprecision-aware Reconstruction of Clinical Annals.

🔍 Overview

CliniCIRCA is the first framework to temporally classify clinical events across unstructured discharge summaries that lack event-level timestamps.

🧩 How it works

The framework operates through a multi-stage process:

  • Event Extraction and Tagging: The system identifies events and applies temporal tags.
  • Clinician-in-the-loop Evaluation: Verified gold-standard labels are produced by correcting errors identified by clinicians.
  • Temporally Grounded Summarization: Corrected timelines are used to compress source material by 1.52 times into chronological records grouped by date.

⚙️ Key details

  • Data Source: 14,882 MIMIC-III mental health admissions.
  • Benchmark: A benchmark of 52 discharge summaries resulted in 15,891 temporally tagged events, with 629 errors corrected by clinicians.
  • Scaling: The framework generated 1,000 silver-standard timelines to be evaluated as training data.
  • Performance: Instruction tuning generally improved five open-weight models across event extraction, temporal tagging, and summarization when compared with few-shot and zero-shot prompting.

#LLM #ClinicalAI #Healthcare #MIMIC-III

Source: CliniCIRCA: A Modular LLM Framework for Constructing Longitudinal Mental Health Patient Journeys from Raw EHR Narratives

item.title: SA Health Apologises for Patient Transfer Delays in Mount Gambier
item.description:
SA Health Apologises for Patient Transfer Delays in Mount Gambier

SA Health has issued an apology for significant delays experienced by a patient during a transfer from Mount Gambier to Adelaide.

🔍 Overview

A patient, Patrick Rainford, suffered a broken hip and faced extended wait times during his transfer from Mount Gambier Hospital to Flinders Medical Centre in Adelaide. The delays occurred during overnight holding for imaging, air transfer, and upon arrival in Adelaide.

⚙️ Key details

  • Patient held overnight in Mount Gambier for x-ray imaging before transfer decision
  • Flown to Adelaide the following day via Royal Flying Doctors
  • Reported hours-long wait at airport facility and further ‘ramping’ delays at Flinders Medical Centre
  • SA Health CEO Robyn Lawrence confirmed trained staff were present during the transfer process

💬 Official response

SA Health chief executive Robyn Lawrence stated: ‘Trained staff were on hand during the transfer.’

#Healthcare #PatientTransfer #SAHealth

Source: South East SA local news briefing

item.title: Saudi Arabia and Portugal Strengthen Healthcare Cooperation During Ministerial Visit
item.description:
Saudi Arabia and Portugal Strengthen Healthcare Cooperation During Ministerial Visit

Saudi Arabia’s Health Minister, Fahad Al-Jalajel, has begun an official visit to Portugal aimed at strengthening bilateral healthcare cooperation. The visit focuses on expanding relations, exchanging expertise, and exploring collaborative opportunities across the health sector.

🔍 Overview

During the official visit, Minister Al-Jalajel is scheduled to meet with senior officials and representatives from Portugal’s health sector. These meetings are designed to examine how closer cooperation and knowledge sharing can support the development of health systems, services, and innovation in both Saudi Arabia and Portugal.

⚙️ Key Focus Areas

The bilateral exchange centers on several main elements:

  • Healthcare Transformation: A key focus is Saudi Arabia’s ongoing healthcare transformation, with the Saudi delegation highlighting progress and lessons learned from their system’s development.
  • Knowledge and Expertise Sharing: The exchange is intended to facilitate the transfer of knowledge and identify areas of mutual interest to build stronger health systems.
  • Portuguese Insights: The Saudi delegation aims to learn about Portuguese approaches to healthcare delivery, system development, and innovation.
  • Institutional Collaboration: By engaging health authorities and sector leaders, both nations seek to establish practical opportunities for collaboration and strengthen institutional links.

💡 Why It Matters

This visit underscores the rising importance of international partnerships in addressing the changing demands of modern healthcare systems. Through these discussions, both nations seek to:

  • Improve healthcare service delivery and encourage innovation.
  • Strengthen the overall efficiency and resilience of their health sectors.
  • Provide Saudi Arabia with opportunities to exchange experiences regarding healthcare transformation.
  • Enable Portugal to build on its relationship with Saudi Arabia and explore cooperative efforts that support shared interests.

#SaudiArabia #Portugal #Healthcare #BilateralRelations #HealthInnovation

Source: Saudi Arabia Portugal Healthcare Cooperation Expands During Ministerial Visit

item.title: MobiCHAI’3 Workshop Focuses on Trustworthy AI for Cognitive Support
item.description:
MobiCHAI’3 Workshop Focuses on Trustworthy AI for Cognitive Support

The ACM International Conference on Mobile Human-Computer Interaction 2026 will host the 3rd International Workshop on Mobile Cognition-Altering and Cognitive-Augmenting Technologies using Human-Centered AI (mobiCHAI’3).

🔍 Overview

  • MobiCHAI’3 is the third edition of the International Workshop on Mobile Cognition-Altering/Augmenting Technologies (CAT) Using Human-Centered AI.
  • The workshop follows two successful events in 2024 and 2025.
  • Organizers include Agnes Gruenerbl, Jan Spilski, Paul Lukowicz, and Thomas Lachmann, all affiliated with institutions in Kaiserslautern, Germany.

⚙️ Key details

  • The focus has shifted from exploring the design space to trustworthy, mission-oriented, and domain-specific mobile and wearable AI systems for cognitive support in real-world contexts.
  • Key domains include healthcare and other high-stakes areas, such as:
    • Support for surgical preparation and perioperative procedures
    • Monitoring of stress and workload
    • Cognitive assistance for clinicians and care teams
  • Special attention is given to trust calibration in AI-supported decision-making.
  • Contributions are welcome from education, work, accessibility, well-being, and everyday life.

🧩 Topics

  • Multimodal sensing of cognitive and affective states
  • Human-centered modeling and simulation of cognition
  • Methods of cognitive augmentation
  • Ethical, social, and trust-related implications

🎓 Audience

  • The conference addresses an interdisciplinary community spanning:
    • Mobile HCI
    • Ubiquitous Computing
    • Cognitive Science
    • Healthcare
    • AI
    • Design Research
    • Social Sciences

#AI #MobileHCI #CognitiveAugmentation #HumanCenteredAI #Healthcare #TrustworthyAI

Source: Program at a Glance - MobileHCI 2026

item.title: AI Detects Heart Disease in Women Through Mammograms
item.description:
AI Detects Heart Disease in Women Through Mammograms

A new study suggests that artificial intelligence (AI) can identify heart disease in women by analysing mammogram images.

🔍 Overview

  • AI can detect heart disease in women using mammograms, study suggests.

⚙️ Key details

  • The capability is demonstrated in a research study.
  • It targets female patients.
  • The analysis is performed on existing mammogram scans.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a potential method for early heart disease detection in women.
  • Utilises imaging already performed for breast cancer screening, offering additional health insights without extra procedures.

#AI #Healthcare #WomenHealth #MedicalAI

Source: AI (artificial intelligence)
